title: Modern Route-Full Stack GenerativeAI And Agentic AI Bootcamp
_comment_title: Copied exactly as published, including 'GenerativeAI' as one word and the hyphen after 'Route'. The overview block on the same page calls it 'Full Stack Generative Ai Bootcamp' — that is a second, informal name for the same program, not a different course.
_comment_overview: PARAPHRASED from the sponsor's page — never copy marketing prose verbatim. Facts (6 months, 16 modules, live weekend cohort, ₹8000, two capstones) are used as-is; the wording is rewritten. The page's 'not a prompting-only course' framing is intentionally not reproduced.
overview: A six-month live weekend bootcamp covering the full generative AI stack end to end: transformer foundations, model selection, LLM APIs, PEFT fine-tuning, production RAG, agent and multi-agent orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, and deployment on AWS. Sixteen modules run from tokenization and embeddings through to containerized services with CI/CD and observability. It closes with two deployed capstones — a citation-backed document intelligence portal and an autonomous multi-agent report generation system.
_comment_category: Primary is GenAI / LLM Engineering, not Agentic AI, despite the title naming both. Weight the syllabus: modules 1-8 and 10-13 are LLM foundations, fine-tuning, RAG, evaluation and cloud; agents are modules 9, 12 and 14 plus one of the two capstones. Category drives the B3 diversity cap (≤3 of 5 recs from one bucket), and the catalog already has two Agentic AI primaries — filing this one where it actually belongs keeps that cap meaningful instead of gaming it.
_comment_level: 'Beginner' here means new to LLMs, NOT new to programming — the page targets 'AI engineers, software developers, and tech professionals' and starts at transformer architecture, not at Python syntax. Span is real (module 1 is tokenization; module 16 is a deployed multi-agent system), so level_range is recorded, but it is stored only and NOT scored today; `level` = intermediate has to stand alone as the fusion anchor.
_comment_prereqs: No prerequisite is stated anywhere on the page and no named prior course is referenced, so `prereq_ids` is empty by evidence rather than by omission. The implied entry condition is working software-engineering experience plus Python.
_comment_price: ₹8000.00 stated as 'incl. GST' — this is the all-in figure a buyer pays, so it is stored as-is with no tax adjustment. Band 'mid' per §2 (3,000-9,999). Own-site cohort pricing, not coupon-driven, so a number is safe here (unlike the Udemy files).
_comment_rating: No star rating or review count appears on the page. Null, not guessed — the validator's null-rating warning is expected and is the point.

format._comment_duration: The cohort badge says '6 Months'; the overview prose on the same page says '5-6 month'. Stored the badge figure as the committed calendar length and recording the disagreement here per §7 — it is marketing softness, not a version skew.
format._comment_duration_hours: Null by design — this is a live cohort, not on-demand video. No total content-hours figure is published.
format._comment_cohort_start: NULL ON PURPOSE — THIS IS THE KEY JUDGMENT IN THIS FILE. The only cohort the page advertises starts 15 March 2026, which is in the PAST as of the 6 Aug 2026 curation date (~5 months into a 6-month program). §3 makes a past date in `cohort_start` the single most dangerous defect in the schema, because generate reads that field as a live persuasion fact and would tell a user today to enroll for a cohort that is nearly over. Value moved to top-level `cohort_start_stale`. Consequence is deliberate: freshness.py's demotion rule scores this live course at the `recorded` mode prior (0.45) because recordings of a mostly-finished cohort is operationally what a buyer gets today; `declared_mode` stays 'live' so the card can still truthfully say 'live bootcamp'. When the next cohort is announced, put that date here and freshness recovers on real evidence.
format._comment_enrollment_status: 'open' because the page still renders an active Enroll Now CTA — that is the observable evidence. I considered 'closed' on the reasoning that a 6-month cohort begun in March 2026 can no longer be meaningfully joined in August, but that would be inference stacked on top of a penalty the scorer already applies: the stale-cohort demotion above has independently dropped the mode prior from 1.00 to 0.45. Adding the 0.25 closed multiplier would double-charge this course for one fact. Revisit if the CTA disappears or a waitlist appears.
format._comment_dates: Neither a publish date nor an 'updated' badge is on the page. Both null rather than guessed. Recency therefore falls through to `cohort_start_stale` (2026-03-15) under §6's fallback chain, which is ~5 months old and scores around 0.76 on the 365-day half-life — an honest, evidence-backed number rather than the 0.35 unknown floor.
format._comment_curriculum_version: The page publishes no version string. Null per §7. Content is clearly current-generation (MCP, deep agents, GRPO, vectorless-era RAG tooling), but 'clearly recent' is not a version number and must not be invented as one.

_comment_perks: The page has no 'what's included' box, so these are the only three benefits it actually states. perks is Tier 3 and is injected verbatim into the generate prompt, so nothing inferred (community access, job support, dashboard access, recordings) was added — the sibling course advertises those explicitly and this one does not.
_comment_objectives: §1 corroboration rule applied, and it caught one. The 'What You Will Learn' block promises deployment on 'AWS/Azure' and repeats 'Azure equivalents' in the Why-Us section, but the 16-module curriculum has exactly one cloud module — 'Module 13: Cloud Services for GenAI - Amazon Web Services (AWS)' — and no Azure content anywhere. The Azure claim is dropped, not softened: validate cites objectives back to users as reasons, so an uncorroborated one is a lie with a citation attached. The eight kept objectives each map to a named module (1-2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10-11, 13).
objectives: Understand transformer architecture, tokenization, embeddings and vector similarity as the foundations of modern LLMs
Choose the right model for a task by comparing LLMs, SLMs and multimodal families on cost, latency, modality and deployment feasibility
Build production LLM API integrations with streaming, retries, token and cost tracking, and provider-agnostic abstraction layers
Adapt models to your own domain with parameter-efficient fine-tuning using LoRA, QLoRA and Hugging Face PEFT tooling
Build grounded, citation-backed RAG systems with chunking strategy, vector databases, metadata filtering, MMR and cross-encoder re-ranking
Take RAG to production with context engineering, caching, multimodal retrieval and reliability evaluation of faithfulness and relevance
Design single-agent and multi-agent systems with supervisor and hierarchical patterns, tool use, memory, and human-in-the-loop approvals
Ship safe GenAI services with guardrails, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, observability, and containerized deployment on AWS with CI/CD
objectives_dropped: Deploy and scale GenAI systems on Azure (advertised as 'AWS/Azure' and 'Azure equivalents', but no Azure module exists in the 16-module curriculum)
_comment_modules: 16 published modules clustered into 10 THEMATIC groups per §4 — never one chunk per module. Detail level is uneven in the source and that is reflected honestly: only Module 1's five lectures were published individually, so its `modules` entries are real lecture titles, while the other groups' entries are drawn from the module names plus the matching 'What You Will Learn' descriptions on the same page. Nothing here is invented; where the page gave only a module title, the entry stays at that granularity.

_comment_projects: Only two projects, but both are full deployments rather than notebook demos, and they are the course's strongest differentiator against the other agentic bootcamps in the catalog — hence the unusually long descriptions. projects is a single embedded chunk (§4), so the detail costs one vector, not two.
skills: Model selection (LLM vs SLM vs multimodal)
_comment_skills: Two edits to the published 'Skills You Will Acquire' list. (1) NORMALISED — several published entries are sentences ('Model Selection Strategy (Cost/Latency/Use-case)', 'Streaming Responses & API Optimisation'); §1 wants concrete named technologies, so near-duplicates were merged and the AWS services collapsed into one entry. Result is 30 entries, right at the validator's warn threshold, which is a fair reflection of a 16-module full-stack program.
